PullRequest.Title: chat: improve Draw persistent progress animation
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- replace the legacy clip-path Draw motion with a smooth folded-ribbon animation while keeping the existing `Draw`, `Draw (Monochrome)`, and `Draw (Monochrome, No Icon)` setting values
- preserve the exact VS Code mark, product colors, compact footprint, live setting changes, and reduced-motion behavior
- use mirrored cubic position curves for parabolic velocity: fast load-in, zero-velocity hold, accelerating unravel, then a short clean rest
- keep generated geometry mask-only so the visible edges remain the existing production SVG paths
- make component fixtures drive RAF motion through the shared Enable Animations control and validate it separately from CSS animations

## Testing

- `npm run compile`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatWorkingLogo.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatConfiguration.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts` (565 passing, 1 pre-existing pending)
- targeted ESLint and Stylelint
- all 24 Draw/monochrome/no-icon animated and reduced-motion chat fixtures rendered headlessly
- standalone Draw fixture verified moving → assembled static → moving through the live Enable Animations control
- manual validation in the Agents window at the production 12px size

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The RAF loop, active-response ownership, default-on Insiders configuration, geometry call chain, and removed CSS implementation are all explicit in the changed code. Exact milliseconds vary by refresh rate and machine, but the new main-thread work and its scaling are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Per-frame CPU work, transient arrays/Maps/path strings, SVG path parsing, and mask rasterization.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with display refresh rate × active Draw-logo count × response duration. RAF runs for 100% of the active lifetime; geometry and strings are rebuilt during 80% of each 4-second cycle, and independent logos have no shared scheduler or frame cache.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Continuous main-thread CPU/GC pressure and SVG repaint work on the frame critical path, with increased risk of dropped frames and input latency.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: An active logo used three browser-managed CSS clip-path animations over fixed SVG paths. Application JavaScript did not wake each frame, construct path geometry or strings, update SVG attributes, or force dynamic SVG-mask painting.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each active Draw logo now runs JavaScript every display frame, rebuilds ribbon geometry and path strings during 80% of every 4-second loop, compares the resulting strings only after construction, and mutates SVG mask path data. The previous implementation used three fixed SVG faces animated by browser-managed CSS clip-path keyframes and performed no per-frame application JavaScript or path allocation.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 185 adds a perpetual requestAnimationFrame path that calls renderDrawFrame for each active Draw logo; RIGHT line 193 then invokes the new geometry builder before the next paint. The same diff removes the prior CSS keyframes from chatWorkingLogo.css.
Findings.Title: Bound the Draw animation's per-frame SVG work
Findings.Impact: With Draw enabled (the Insiders default, and available through experiments/settings), every foreground agent response adds continuous main-thread CPU/GC work and SVG mask repainting for its full lifetime. Long-running requests, high-refresh-rate displays, or multiple active chat widgets multiply this work and can reduce editor responsiveness or drop frames while streaming chat.
Findings.Evidence: ChatWorkingProgressContentPart creates one ChatWorkingProgressLogo for the persistent progress row and keeps it active while a response or interaction is pending. renderNextDrawFrame at chatWorkingLogo.ts:185 executes on every RAF and immediately requeues itself. renderDrawFrame calls getChatWorkingLogoDrawFrame; its Ribbon.bands/sections path allocates Maps, arrays, points, and concatenated SVG path strings, including up to the 32-step flattened fold geometry, before the path-data cache can reject unchanged output. setAttribute('d', ...) also reparses and repaints an SVG mask. The removed implementation was fixed SVG geometry plus CSS clip-path keyframes.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the frame path bounded: precompute and share a finite frame table (30 fps is already treated as acceptable in the added tests), advance only when the frame index changes, and pause scheduling through the hold/rest intervals; alternatively restore a declarative CSS/WAAPI mask animation. Avoid rebuilding completed bands and reparsing `d` attributes on every display refresh.

Scenarios.Scenario: Animate persistent progress during an active chat/agent response
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For every active foreground response, requestAnimationFrame calls renderNextDrawFrame before paint, synchronously generates geometry/strings, mutates an SVG mask path when its moving band changes, and then schedules the next frame. This work is directly on the rendering critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Generate ribbon paths and write SVG mask `d` attributes from requestAnimationFrame.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At 60 Hz, 60 JavaScript callbacks per second per active logo; during 80% of each 4-second loop, geometry is rebuilt each callback and approximately one moving band's `d` attribute changes per callback. Cardinality doubles on a 120 Hz display and multiplies by active logos.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Three fixed SVG faces used CSS clip-path keyframes. The application performed no per-frame JavaScript geometry/string construction or SVG attribute writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Geometry allocation, SVG path parsing, mask rasterization, and repaint must occur for the animation frame and compete with editor input and chat streaming work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Display refresh rate, duration of the active response, and number of simultaneously active Draw logos. Draw is the Insiders default and can also be enabled by experiment or user setting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One independent RAF loop per active logo with no shared scheduler or limiter. A typical widget has one active persistent-progress logo; concurrent chat widgets/windows scale the work linearly. Browser background RAF throttling can reduce work only when the whole target window is not foreground.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The ribbon model plus fully tied/empty paths are module-level singletons, and artwork is created lazily per Draw logo. Moving frames are not cached: Ribbon.bands reconstructs Maps, arrays, points, and path strings every time; the per-band string cache is consulted only after reconstruction. Independent logos do not share generated frames.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added RAF loop, full geometry call chain, active-response lifetime, and removed CSS keyframes are explicit in the diff and callers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame cost depends on Chromium, device speed, refresh rate, and active-logo count; no benchmark is supplied. The persistent main-thread path and multiplicative scaling are certain, so magnitude uncertainty is reflected in medium severity rather than suppressing the finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: the diff replaces browser-managed CSS motion with continuous main-thread geometry allocation and dynamic SVG-mask painting.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch progress style, reduce motion, stop, complete, or dispose a logo
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A setting/reduced-motion change synchronously cancels the pending frame and renders at most one initial or tied frame. Completion/disposal cancels the MutableDisposable frame. This is event-driven rather than a sustained hot path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create Draw SVG masks and render the initial/static frame.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One-time creation of three mask paths/faces per logo on the first switch to Draw, followed by at most three SVG `d` writes for the static frame.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The three fixed face wrappers/SVGs were created eagerly in the logo constructor; switching styles only changed classes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous DOM/SVG construction occurs during the setting or state transition, but it is bounded and not repeated after artwork exists.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live logos affected by a setting or accessibility change, normally one per active response.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One event per affected logo; configuration and accessibility-service events fan out to currently instantiated logos, but normal use has one per active response and no expensive asynchronous boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Draw artwork is created once when first selected and retained for the logo. The tied frame is precomputed globally and reused; reduced motion, inactive state, and No Icon/Off do not retain a live RAF. Configuration changes reuse existing artwork.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: cancellation, lazy creation, and reduced-motion branches are directly implemented and covered by changed tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The one-time SVG construction cost is small and bounded; no evidence indicates visible transition latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: cleanup cancels scheduled work, reduced/no-icon/off states do not animate, and one-time lazy SVG construction is bounded.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Only component-fixture rendering and the fixture's Enable Animations control reach this path; it is outside product workflows.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fan out animation-enable changes to fixture subscribers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One synchronous event per fixture logo per Enable Animations toggle; subsequent RAF work follows the logo animation behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The control only toggled a CSS class and did not notify JavaScript animations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can affect fixture rendering only, not end-user editor progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of logo instances in a component fixture gallery.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The fixture control synchronously notifies all rendered fixture logos, each of which independently restarts or stops its RAF. Concurrency is bounded by the fixture's small predefined gallery.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The component fixture adds one shared emitter and each fixture logo subscribes once. Gallery logos retain their normal per-instance animation state; no production cache or lifecycle changes are reached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed listeners and call sites are under componentFixtures.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Fixture-only cost is not user-visible and the gallery cardinality is fixed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No product performance finding: the fan-out is test/development-only and bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open accessibility help or migrate the legacy `ribbon` setting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accessibility-help string assembly occurs only when help is requested; configuration migration is one-time configuration processing. Neither reaches subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One help invocation or one migrated setting value; input cardinality is constant.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single invocation per help request or migration; no queue or burst behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No caches, collection scans, or repeated expensive operations were added by the accessibility text and configuration migration changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High after inspecting the complete changed hunks and their direct configuration context.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; changes add a short string fragment and one constant-time legacy-value comparison.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: both changes are constant-time, infrequent metadata/configuration work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and traced active-response rendering, configuration/reduced-motion lifecycle, fixture animation controls, and metadata/migration paths. Submitted one medium-severity synchronous UI/rendering finding for the new unbounded per-display-frame SVG geometry path; cleanup and non-animated states are bounded, and no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundaries were introduced.
